comment: Queued work for the ai-skills repository. Schema: todo/SKILL.md. Kept sorted by priority. created_at was backfilled at 2026-08-20 for rows that predate the field.

tasks.title: ai-text-editor: syntax-check every edit and warn of breakage; refuse save on new errors until acknowledged
tasks.detail: Agents editing through ai-text-editor (the editor gate forces every edit there) break code often -- a closing brace lost in a replace, two lines deleted with a scene block -- and see it only several calls later when the page or build throws, because unlike native Edit the editor surfaces no diagnostics. Agreed design (Tschallacka, 2026-11-13, Q3a/Q4a/Q5b): (1) run a check on every insert/replace/bulk_edit against the in-memory buffer, before save, and report it in that edit's own response; (2) report only errors the edit INTRODUCED (diagnostics before vs after, near the edited range), so a file already broken does not nag on every edit; a transaction checks once at end_transaction; (3) save is refused while edit-introduced syntax errors stand, until the caller passes an explicit acknowledgement. Phase 1: cheap per-language checkers, no daemon -- node --check (js/mjs/cjs), php -l, bash -n, python3 -m py_compile, the editor's own JSON/XML parsers. Phase 2: warm per-language LSPs held by the editor server for what checkers cannot cover (inline <script> in HTML via vscode-html-language-server, CSS, YAML, Vue, TS), discovered on PATH, filtered to syntax-class diagnostics, with a timeout that reports 'check pending' instead of blocking the edit. Absent tooling degrades to 'unchecked', never to a refusal.

tasks.title: benchmark/skill-adoption prepare-cell.sh silently ships a skill dir with no binary unless staged by hand
tasks.detail: prepare-cell.sh's disposable install only works if <skill>/bin/<triple>/<binary> is already staged for every dual-surface skill (ai-text-editor, chat, decisions, tailpipe) before the installer copies it -- setup-dev-env.sh only stages interactive-shell's own bin/<triple>/, not these. Two independent live-experiment agents (running real cells against S01-ai-text-editor and S04-decisions) each had to manually mirror installer/build-release.sh's own copy convention by hand before a cell would actually have a working binary, with no warning from prepare-cell.sh when the staging step was missing. Confirms PROTOCOL.md's own open caveat that the installer invocation is unverified end-to-end against a disposable HOME.

tasks.title: ai-text-editor-server: idle watchdog should consult 'claude agents --json' before self-terminating
tasks.detail: The idle watchdog (spawn_idle_watchdog, src/ai-text-editor/src/bin/ai-text-editor-server.rs) self-terminates purely on elapsed wall-clock inactivity (default 600s) plus in-flight/detached-job checks -- it has no signal for whether the owning chat session is still open. A session that is simply busy elsewhere (not touching this file) for 10+ minutes loses its editor server and gets a new tab generation on the next reconnect, which is the precondition for B3's stale-registry-row race (shrinks how often it's hit, does not close the window itself -- that's B3's own exit-path-ordering defect). Fix (MCP installs only; no equivalent for CLI-only installs, which have no long-lived owning process to check): 'claude agents --json' is a documented, scriptable command (--help: 'Print active sessions (interactive and background) as a JSON array and exit (for scripting; does not require a TTY)') that returns each live session's sessionId and pid. The server already knows its own agent_id (the same value, via agent_session_key::resolve_session_key) from registration. The watchdog should shell out to 'claude agents --json' on each poll and skip the idle-exit if its own agent_id is still present as a sessionId in the result, regardless of elapsed idle time.
tasks.note: Implemented in the same commit as B3 (094f51e8): the idle watchdog now computes current_agent_id() and, right before honoring the idle timeout, shells out to 'claude agents --json' (owning_session_is_alive); if the agent_id is still listed, the watchdog continues instead of exiting. Pure matching logic (agent_is_listed) unit-tested directly (6 cases: listed, unlisted, empty list, malformed JSON, object-instead-of-array, entry missing sessionId). The subprocess-calling half is not unit-tested (no fake 'claude' binary substituted); behavior when 'claude' is missing or errors is to fall back to the existing timeout unchanged, by design.
